english.title: Immigration - enter / remain in UK beyond time limit
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), not being a British citizen and having only a limited leave to enter or remain in the United Kingdom, knowingly remained beyond the time limited by the leave
english.legislation: Contrary to section 24(1)(b)(i) of the Immigration Act 1971.

english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies from the 27th June 2022 due to changes made by the Nationality and Borders Act 2022. The replacement offence is provided for in section 24(C1) and (F1) of the Immigration Act 1971, see H100695.(ii) The offence is committed on the day the person first knows that the time limited by the leave has expired and continues during the period in the United Kingdom thereafter.
(iii) A person can only be prosecuted once in respect of the same limited leave (section 24(1A)).
(iv) The term alien is used in the actual legislation. Therefore it would be inappropriate to change the wording in the offence wording. In day to day speech the term 'foreign national' is more acceptable.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, not being a British citizen and having only a limited leave to enter or remain in the United Kingdom, knowingly remained beyond the time limited by the leave.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant

By section 28A of the Immigration Act 1971 (as amended by the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999) an immigration official may arrest without warrant a person who has committed or attempted to commit an offence under section 24 or section 24A of the Immigration Act 1971.
other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
36 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
